findings: makePlugin replaces validateMount with a null-return spy and path warnings with empty lists. Tests which explicitly restore validation exercise the real validator, but ordinary fallback and ownership tests do not establish complete admission/path policy.

Most filesystem writes/reads are independent spies; selected managed-TOC edit tests instead use a shared document string. The specific binding-destination test uses independent reads after writes, so previous stateful isolated overwrite controls are not contradicted.

Progress tests replace replayMountContentsToVault with a fixed result, and hides-notice-on-reject mocks a rejected top-level replay. They do not exercise the internally caught stat error and success-style partial completion reproduced by v25.

Pending-probe, pending-list, source-switch, Disable, unload and same-ID edit-queue tests assert concrete stale-state guards using deferred promises and mock file maps. They are useful unit contracts, not native Obsidian event ordering or filesystem transaction evidence.

Recorded private vault handler is evaluated under vm with synthetic TFile/TFolder and stat/cache/event state; host version provenance absent. Exact modify/raw assertions do not establish current/oldest-host editor, Outline, metadata or save compatibility.

SFTP trust persistence cases cover save-waiting, changed/reset/stale/concurrent keys, cancellation, abort, pin rollback and ordinary edits using synthetic fingerprints and modal buttons. These are separate from the seven real-loopback test implementations reviewed earlier; neither suite rerun here.
Remote root-trash cases cancel mocked dialogs before backend operations and assert no saved deletion choice. They cover UI exclusion/cancellation, not live provider deletion or native trash behavior.

Windows path expectations include POSIX write paths and /linux/custom.json after host path.join; this agrees with documented four Windows baseline failures. No new supported-platform run or waiver established.
